topic: Questions to ask before authorizing any repair — REEL-SLATE-2026-07-31 topic #20
mechanicTruth: The shop's actual written policy is: never quote a repair beyond the fixed prices blind — free check, written quote, customer approves before any work begins.
driverConfusion: Drivers often don't know they're allowed to ask to see the failed part, ask what happens if they wait, ask whether a repair is safety-critical vs. routine, or ask to keep the old part — so they either overpay or under-question a real safety issue.
clevelandAngle: None specific — evergreen consumer-trust content, tied to the shop's Euclid Ave location only via the CTA card, not the core claim.

voiceoverScript.line: You're allowed to ask these - before you say yes to any repair.
Any shop, not just this one.
One. Can you show me the part?
Two. What happens if I wait?
Three. Is this safety, or is it maintenance?
Four. Can I have the old part back?
A good shop won't flinch. Free check, written quote - you don't pay until you say yes.
Save this. Bring it to your next appointment - anywhere.
